article.description:
Tamika Catchings hit a 15-footer from the left baseline to give Indiana
the lead with 45 seconds left, had a season-high 31 points and led
the Fever to their 13th straight home win, 76-69 over the New York
Liberty on Thursday night.
article.headline: Indiana erases 18-point hole en route to win
article.linkText: Catchings, Fever post big rally to edge Liberty
article.story:
INDIANAPOLIS (AP) -- The Indiana Fever needed Tamika Catchings to
stay perfect at home.

	   As usual, she delivered.

	   Catchings hit a 15-footer from the left baseline to give Indiana
the lead with 45 seconds left, had a season-high 31 points and led
the Fever to their 13th straight home win, 76-69 over the New York
Liberty on Thursday night.

	   "The last time I remember everything going in like that was
when I tore my ACL,'' she said.

	   There was no such misfortune this time.

	   Catchings was 11-of-20 from the field, including 5-of-8 from
3-point range, and grabbed six rebounds in playing like the Eastern
Conference's leading vote-getter for Saturday's All-Star game.

	   This victory, however, did not come by design.

	   The seven-point margin was the slimmest the Fever (10-7) have
had at home this season. It also required rallying from an 18-point
first-half deficit -- the second largest comeback in franchise
history.

	   Indiana trailed by 19 points before beating Phoenix 86-78 on
July 1, 2001.

	   The league's only unbeaten team at home now has the WNBA's
third-longest home winning streak, and Catchings was the primary
reason the Fever extended it Thursday.

	   She got the Fever out of an early funk by hitting consecutive
3-pointers after New York had taken a 22-4 lead.

	   She scored 11 straight points in a 4:41 stretch when Indiana and
New York were trading leads late.

	   She hit the 15-footer with 45 seconds left to give Indiana the
lead for good and even connected on a buzzer-beating 3-pointer to
finish one point short of her career-high

	   Catchings also shut down Liberty guard Vickie Johnson after she
scored 14 points in the first 7:12. Johnson finished with 22 points
to lead the Liberty (7-7), while Elena Baranova added 12 points and
12 rebounds.

	   New York played without All-Star center Tari Phillips, who had a
family emergency in Florida. A team spokesman said Phillips is
expected back for the All-Star game, and it was clear that New York
missed her.

	   "Our offensive sets broke down,'' New York coach Richie Adubato
said. "Tamika made big shots at the end.''

	   Without Catchings, the Fever looked ordinary.

	   New York took advantage by grabbing the big lead early and still
led 40-31 at halftime after Catchings drew her third foul with 3:54
to go.

	   The second half was a different story.

	   Indiana's Coretta Brown started the rally by hitting a
3-pointer, a 5-foot runner and a breakaway layup. Natalie Williams
followed that with a tip-in to make it 42-40 less than three
minutes into the second half.

	   Then Catchings got going.

	   "It was a team effort,'' Brown said. "Having Tamika stepping
up, like she always does, makes it much better.''

	   Catchings gave Indiana its first lead, at 49-46 with 12:45 to
go, when she completed a three-point play.

	   With Indiana trailing 69-68 in the final minute and the
home-court streak at stake, Catchings did what she does best -- spun
away from a defender to get open and knocked down the 15-footer
from the left baseline for the lead.

	   New York had a chance to retake the lead but Baranova missed a
shot from the top of the key.

	   The Fever sealed the victory with three free throws -- and
Catchings' buzzer-beating 21-footer.

	   "It was about just waking up,'' Catchings said. "We just stuck
together.''
